task.description:
FINAL REWORK (3/3) -- if this also FAILs at re-gate, ORCH escalates per docs/agents/ORCHESTRATOR.md Section 5 rather than attempting a 4th rework. Read handoffs/WF03-ISS0736-20260921/step-02b-code-design-validator-rework2.json's result.summary in full for the exact FAIL: the 3 previously-failing tests all assert `roles == ["VIEWER"]`, and "VIEWER" is NOT a member of Letflow.Api.Authorization.role()'s closed type (:PLATFORM_ADMIN | :PROCESS_DESIGNER | :PROCESS_OPERATOR | :TASK_WORKER | :AGENT_RUNNER | :CANDIDATE, lib/letflow/api/authorization.ex:195-201), so §2.2's group-resolution step correctly finds zero matching tenant_role rows for it and writes nothing to group_members -- meaning under the new design these 3 tests' literal `roles == ["VIEWER"]` assertion would now read `roles == []`.

ORCH's own investigation (do not re-derive from scratch, verify instead): read test/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline_integration_test.exs lines ~110-130 directly -- its own comment already states 'token double mints role "VIEWER" -- not a recognised Letflow.Api.Authorization.role(), so roles_from_strings/1 drops it and the caller holds no role at all.' That is: even BEFORE this run's fix, an unrecognized claimed role like "VIEWER" never granted any actual permission -- Letflow.Api.Authorization.roles_from_strings/1 (lib/letflow/api/authorization.ex:408-409) already filters conn.assigns.auth_context.roles down to the closed role() set before any access decision is made. `conn.assigns.auth_context.roles` containing the raw unrecognized string was ALWAYS an audit/observability artifact of the old pure-JWT-pass-through implementation, never a security-relevant value in its own right -- the 403 all 3 tests assert comes from roles_from_strings/1 dropping "VIEWER" to an empty granted-role set, not from the literal list contents.

Your job: verify this reasoning is actually correct (read roles_from_strings/1's real implementation and confirm it behaves as described; confirm evaluate_access/2 is the only consumer of auth_context.roles for the actual access decision), and if confirmed, write it into the design doc as an explicit new subsection (e.g. §2.3 'Test-assertion impact') stating: (a) this requirement's whole point is that the closed-set, permission-granting portion of the role list must come from live Letflow-local state, not raw JWT claims -- an unrecognized/unmapped claim string was already inert for authorization purposes and its presence or absence in the raw list is not a security property; (b) therefore the new design correctly changes what conn.assigns.auth_context.roles contains (only DB-backed group-derived names, dropping claim strings with no local backing) and this is an intentional, in-scope consequence of REQ-378's contract change, not a regression; (c) name the exact 3 pre-existing test files and state precisely what changes in each (the literal expected value each assertion must change to, e.g. `roles == []` where currently `roles == ["VIEWER"]`, while every other assertion in each test -- especially the 403 status code and any other proof-of-pipeline-execution assertions -- stays unchanged, since the deny outcome is unaffected); (d) confirm this test-assertion update is authorized as part of REQ-378's implementation (not a separate TEST-DESIGNER task, since it is editing 3 pre-existing regression tests' literal expected values to match a deliberately changed, in-spec contract, not adding new coverage) and can be done by ELIXIR-DEV directly in the next implementation step. If your own verification of roles_from_strings/1 or evaluate_access/2 contradicts this reasoning, say so explicitly and design the actual correct fix instead -- do not force this conclusion if the source doesn't support it.
acceptance_criteria: roles_from_strings/1 and evaluate_access/2's actual behavior independently verified against source, not assumed
If reasoning holds: design doc explicitly names all 3 test files and their exact required assertion changes, and confirms this is in-scope for ELIXIR-DEV to implement directly
If reasoning does NOT hold: an alternative, concrete design fix is provided instead -- do not submit a design that still fails the 3 tests without addressing why
No implementation bodies in the design doc itself
